title: ❤️ The Cardiac Cycle
author: Kukui sample content

slides.title: What is the cardiac cycle?
slides.body:
The cardiac cycle is the sequence of events in a single heartbeat: the alternating contraction (systole) and relaxation (diastole) of the heart's chambers that move blood through the circulation.

Over the next few slides we will walk through the phases, then check your understanding.

slides.title: Systole and diastole
slides.body:
• Atrial systole — the atria contract, topping off the ventricles.
  • Ventricular systole — the ventricles contract, ejecting blood into the aorta and pulmonary artery.
  • Diastole — the chambers relax and refill.

The valves open and close in response to pressure changes, producing the familiar “lub-dub” heart sounds.

slides.title: Check: heart sounds
slides.body: Think about which valves are involved in the first heart sound before you answer.

config.title: The first heart sound (S1)
config.question: The first heart sound (“lub”) is produced primarily by the closure of which valves?

answers.feedback: Not quite — closure of the semilunar valves produces the second heart sound (S2), the “dub.”
Correct — S1 marks the start of ventricular systole as the AV valves snap shut.
Not quite — these valves close at different points in the cycle, so they do not produce a single combined sound.

config.title: Phases of the cycle
config.text: During *systole* the heart muscle contracts, while during *diastole* it relaxes and refills with blood.

slides.body:
You stepped through the cardiac cycle: atrial and ventricular systole, then diastole, with valve closures producing the two heart sounds.
